bytes/byte: Memory is counted in bytes, eight bits each. A 32-bit number takes four bytes, and a 16-bit number takes two.
bytes/w: Training with Adam keeps several numbers for every parameter. First the weights, in 16 bits for fast arithmetic: two bytes.
bytes/g: Then one gradient per weight, also in 16 bits: two more.
bytes/master: Small updates would get lost in 16 bits, so each step updates a 32-bit master copy of the weights: four bytes.
bytes/mv: And Adam's two running averages, m and v, kept in 32 bits: four bytes each.
bytes/total: That is sixteen bytes per parameter. Only two of them are the weights the model computes with.
model/n: Now multiply by the parameter count. A 7 billion parameter model needs sixteen times 7 billion bytes.
model/gb: That is 112 billion bytes: 112 gigabytes, or GB, where a gigabyte is a billion bytes.
model/gpu: A large GPU holds 80 gigabytes. This training state alone fills one and spills into a second.
model/big: Ten times the parameters is ten times the memory: a 70 billion parameter model needs 1,120 gigabytes, fourteen such GPUs.
model/batch: The batch never enters this count. It is sixteen bytes per parameter, whether a step sees one example or a thousand.
